**No Spoon.** The digital rain has been falling behind Squachy since the very first release, and he's been staring at it the whole time. Turns out he wasn't zoning out. Every half a minute or so, one glyph in the rain now falls **red**. Big, slow, and very much not supposed to be there. Tap it. Squachy will say "Whoa. I know kung fu," and then he'll want a coat.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.30.0/docs/no-spoon.gif" width="480" alt="On the digital rain background one glyph falls in red, gets tapped, and Squachy says Whoa, I know kung fu. Then Squachy as TH3 0N3: a near-black violet coat with purple lapels and his shades made round, green code falling inside them. With a Flock camera and an AirTag nearby the code in his lenses turns red. In bullet time a bullet creeps past his head and he ducks under it. A tap on his left lens puts a red pill in it. Picked up, he dangles from the finger bending a spoon. And the payphone screen opens ringing RING RING."></p>

**TH3 0N3.** The eighteenth outfit, picked from a costume lab of six takes and fifteen passes. A long near-black coat with a violet edge, lapels folded back to show purple lining, boots, and his own chunky shades made round, with green code falling inside the lenses. All the Matrix lives in his glasses; the rest of him is the same flat cardboard cutout as every other costume. On the digital rain background his idle chatter starts dropping hints about a glyph that doesn't belong until you get the idea, and once the coat is yours the rain stops sending red ones.

**He sees the Agents.** While he's wearing it, the code in his lenses turns red and runs faster whenever something serious is nearby: trackers (AirTag, Tile, SmartTag, Google's tags), Flock and ALPR cameras, Axon gear, Raven gunshot detectors, card skimmers, hacking tools, fake access points and deauth floods. Doorbells, smart glasses and the rest leave him green. Anything you've ignored or snoozed doesn't count.

**He's got moves.** Every fourteen seconds he drops into bullet time: the code in his lenses freezes, the air ripples, and a bullet creeps past his head. Tap him while it's crossing and he ducks it ("Too slow."). Tap his left lens and a red pill glows in it; his right lens, a blue one. Pick him up and he dangles from your finger, calmly bending a spoon. Every few minutes the same black cat walks past behind him twice. And open the payphone (renaming him, or writing to your squad) and it rings for him first. He has eight new lines of his own, too. Free your mind. Keep your Bluetooth off.

**3 KB of RAM back.** The wardriving code was holding two capture queues on every board, 2,948 bytes in all, for a feature only the GPS watch can use. They're only made now on a board that actually wardrives.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- TH3 0N3, a new outfit: tap the red glyph that now and then falls in the DIGITAL rain on the main screen. Hints on DIGITAL while it's locked; the master unlock includes it.
- In TH3 0N3: red lenses while a serious catch is nearby, bullet time every 14 s (tap him to duck), a red or blue pill on a lens tap, a spoon while he's held, a deja vu cat every four minutes, eight lines of his own, and a ringing payphone.

**Changed**
- The squad radio carries nineteen outfit slots. Older boards show a visiting TH3 0N3 as plain Squachy, and a visitor in the coat wears it without the tricks.
- The outfit gallery in the README shows all eighteen costumes.

**Fixed**
- The wardriving capture queues (2,948 bytes of RAM) are made only when wardriving starts, not held on every board.
